question: You are using Vertex AI to manage your ML models and datasets. You recently updated one of your models. You want to track and compare the new version with the previous one and incorporate dataset versioning. What should you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Use Vertex AI TensorBoard to visualize the training metrics of the new model version, and use Data Catalog to manage dataset versioning.

options.label: B
options.text: Use Vertex AI Model Monitoring to monitor the performance of the new model version, and use Vertex AI Training to manage dataset versioning.

options.label: C
options.text: Use Vertex AI Experiments to track and compare model artifacts and versions, and use Vertex ML Metadata to manage dataset versioning.

options.label: D
options.text: Use Vertex AI Experiments to track and compare model artifacts and versions, and use Vertex AI managed datasets to manage dataset versioning.

explanation: Explanation: Vertex AI Experiments is designed to track and compare model versions and their training artifacts, while Vertex ML Metadata manages dataset versioning and lineage, providing an integrated approach to model and dataset version control.

question: You are creating a retraining policy for a customer churn prediction model deployed in Vertex AI. New training data is added weekly. You want to implement a model retraining process that minimizes cost and effort. What should you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Retrain the model when a significant shift in the distribution of customer attributes is detected in the production data compared to the training data.

options.label: B
options.text: Retrain the model when the model's latency increases by 10% due to increased traffic.

options.label: C
options.text: Retrain the model when the model accuracy drops by 10% on the new training dataset.

options.label: D
options.text: Retrain the model every week when new training data is available.

explanation: Explanation: Retraining based on detected significant data distribution shifts ensures the model stays relevant and accurate while minimizing unnecessary retraining costs and effort. This approach is more efficient than retraining on a fixed schedule or solely based on accuracy metrics.

question: You are an AI engineer with an apparel retail company. The sales team has observed seasonal sales patterns over the past 5-6 years. The sales team analyzes and visualizes the weekly sales data stored in CSV files. You have been asked to estimate weekly sales for future seasons to optimize inventory and personnel workloads. You want to use the most efficient approach. What should you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Upload the files into Cloud Storage. Use Python to preprocess and load the tabular data into BigQuery. Use time series forecasting models to predict weekly sales.

options.label: B
options.text: Upload the files into Cloud Storage. Use Python to preprocess and load the tabular data into BigQuery. Train a logistic regression model by using BigQuery ML to predict each product's weekly sales as one of three categories: high, medium, or low.

options.label: C
options.text: Load the files into BigQuery. Preprocess data by using BigQuery SQL. Connect BigQuery to Looker. Create a Looker dashboard that shows weekly sales trends in real time and can slice and dice the data based on relevant filters.

options.label: D
options.text: Create a custom conversational application using Vertex AI Agent Builder. Include code that enables file upload functionality, and upload the files. Use few-shot prompting and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to predict future sales trends by using the Gemini large language model (LLM).

explanation: Explanation: Uploading data to Cloud Storage and then into BigQuery for efficient querying and preprocessing enables scalable data management. Using time series forecasting models on this structured data is the most effective method to predict future weekly sales, capturing seasonal patterns and trends accurately.

question: Your company's business stakeholders want to understand the factors driving customer churn to inform their business strategy. You need to build a customer churn prediction model that prioritizes simple interpretability of your model's results. You need to choose the ML framework and modeling technique that will explain which features led to the prediction. What should you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Build a TensorFlow deep neural network (DNN) model, and use SHAP values for feature importance analysis.

options.label: B
options.text: Build a PyTorch long short-term memory (LSTM) network, and use attention mechanisms for interpretability.

options.label: C
options.text: Build a logistic regression model in scikit-learn, and interpret the model's output coefficients to understand feature impact.

options.label: D
options.text: Build a linear regression model in scikit-learn, and interpret the model's standardized coefficients to understand feature impact.

explanation: Explanation: Logistic regression models provide straightforward interpretability through their coefficients, which directly indicate the impact of each feature on the prediction, making them well-suited for explaining factors driving classification outcomes like customer churn.

question: You are responsible for managing and monitoring a Vertex AI model that is deployed in production. You want to automatically retrain the model when its performance deteriorates. What should you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Create a Vertex AI Model Monitoring job to track the model's performance with production data, and trigger retraining when specific metrics drop below predefined thresholds.

options.label: B
options.text: Collect feedback from end users, and retrain the model based on their assessment of its performance.

options.label: C
options.text: Configure a scheduled job to evaluate the model's performance on a static dataset, and retrain the model if the performance drops below predefined thresholds.

options.label: D
options.text: Use Vertex Explainable AI to analyze feature attributions and identify potential biases in the model. Retrain when significant shifts in feature importance or biases are detected.

explanation: Explanation: Vertex AI Model Monitoring automatically tracks model performance on production data and can be configured to trigger retraining workflows when key metrics fall below defined thresholds, enabling proactive, automated model maintenance.

question: You have developed a custom ML model using Vertex AI and want to deploy it for online serving. You need to optimize the model's serving performance by ensuring that the model can handle high throughput while minimizing latency. You want to use the simplest solution. What should you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Deploy the model to a Vertex AI endpoint resource to automatically scale the serving backend based on the throughput. Configure the endpoint's autoscaling settings to minimize latency.

options.label: B
options.text: Implement a containerized serving solution using Cloud Run. Configure the concurrency settings to handle multiple requests simultaneously.

options.label: C
options.text: Apply simplification techniques such as model pruning and quantization to reduce the model's size and complexity. Retrain the model using Vertex AI to improve its performance, latency, memory, and throughput.

options.label: D
options.text: Enable request-response logging for the model hosted in Vertex AI. Use Looker Studio to analyze the logs, identify bottlenecks, and optimize the model accordingly.

explanation:
⚙️ Vertex AI Endpoint 託管：
模型本身已經在 Vertex AI 開發完成，直接部署至 Vertex AI Endpoint 資源是最原生、維運成本最低且最簡單的解決方案 ⚡。

📈 自動擴展（Autoscaling）機制：
設定 Endpoint 的 Autoscaling 參數後，系統會自動根據當前的吞吐量（Throughput）與請求流量動態調整運算資源，既能處理高流量，又能有效降低延遲並節省成本 💰。
source: PMLE 339 (答案修正版) #336 | explanation corrected on review (Grok | ChatGPT | Gemini)

question: You built a custom Vertex AI pipeline job that preprocesses images and trains an object detection model. The pipeline currently uses 1 n1-standard-8 machine with 1 NVIDIA Tesla V100 GPU. You want to reduce the model training time without compromising model accuracy. What should you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Reduce the number of layers in your object detection model.

options.label: B
options.text: Train the same model on a stratified subset of your dataset.

options.label: C
options.text: Update the WorkerPoolSpec to use a machine with 24 vCPUs and 1 NVIDIA Tesla V100 GPU.

options.label: D
options.text: Update the WorkerPoolSpec to use a machine with 24 vCPUs and 3 NVIDIA Tesla V100 GPUs.

explanation: Explanation: Increasing the number of GPUs while scaling CPU resources allows parallel training, which reduces training time without compromising accuracy. Using 3 NVIDIA Tesla V100 GPUs provides more compute power for efficient model training in Vertex AI Pipelines.

question: You are a SQL analyst. You need to utilize a TensorFlow customer segmentation model stored In Cloud Storage. You want to use the simplest and most efficient approach. What should you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Import the model into Vertex AI Model Registry. Deploy the model to a Vertex AI endpoint, and use SQL for inference in BigQuery.

options.label: B
options.text: Deploy the model by using TensorFlow Serving, and call for inference from BigQuery.

options.label: C
options.text: Convert the model into a BigQuery ML model, and use SQL for inference.

options.label: D
options.text: Import the model into BigQuery, and use SQL for inference.

explanation: Explanation: Importing the TensorFlow model into Vertex AI Model Registry and deploying it to a Vertex AI endpoint allows you to perform scalable, managed online predictions. BigQuery supports making calls to Vertex AI endpoints via SQL functions, enabling simple and efficient inference directly from SQL queries.
source: PMLE 339 (答案修正版) #339 | answer corrected on review

question: You are developing a demand forecasting model for a large online retailer. The company has 20,000 SKUs that are sold through a single distribution center. You have three years of historical data. You need to provide a daily forecast at the SKU level for the next two weeks. You need to develop the first version quickly and minimize the development effort while delivering high forecasting accuracy. What should you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Train a multivariate BigQuery ML ARIMA_PLUS_XREG model on all SKUs by using the TIME_SERIES_ID_COL option.

options.label: B
options.text: Write a Python script in Agent Platform Workbench that trains a BigQuery ML ARIMA model for each SKU, and use a corresponding model for each SKU forecast.

options.label: C
options.text: For each SKU, send the last month’s history of sales and the SKU’s description to Gemini Pro to generate a prediction for the next two weeks. Instruct the LLM to act as a category specialist in retail and to focus on accuracy.

options.label: D
options.text: Fine-tune the Gemini Pro model on the historical data to predict the daily sales for each SKU. Use the fine-tuned model without prompt engineering.

explanation: BigQuery ML can train and manage separate time-series forecasts for all 20,000 SKUs in a single SQL model by using the SKU identifier as TIME_SERIES_ID_COL. ARIMA_PLUS_XREG automates model selection, trend and seasonality handling, and supports additional explanatory variables, providing a scalable, accurate solution with minimal development effort.

question: You work at a manufacturing company. You are building an assistant to help engineers write scripts for a proprietary, legacy machine control language called “MechScript.” MechScript is highly specialized, uses unique syntax not found in public datasets, and is strictly internal to your company. You built the base Gemini model using Agent Platform RAG Engine and grounded the model with the MechScript reference manual. The model correctly answers questions about the language, but it consistently fails to generate syntactically correct code snippets, often hallucinating Python-like syntax instead. What should you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Increase the temperature parameter in the Gemini API call.

options.label: B
options.text: Use the Agent Platform supervised fine-tuning (SFT) service with a dataset of valid MechScript examples.

options.label: C
options.text: Increase the number of retrieved chunks in the RAG Engine call.

options.label: D
options.text: Copy the MechScript manual into the system prompt using Gemini’s context window.

explanation: Supervised fine-tuning with high-quality MechScript input-output examples teaches the model the language’s proprietary syntax and code-generation patterns. RAG supplies reference knowledge at inference time, but fine-tuning is more appropriate when the model must consistently produce outputs in a specialized format that is absent from its original training data.

question: Your company’s data science team has developed a complex feature engineering workflow using Python with pandas that runs on a single Agent Platform Workbench instance. Due to a recent increase in dataset size, the script is failing with out of memory (OOM) errors. You need to scale this workload to run across multiple nodes to handle the data volume. The data science team wants to use Python-native APIs and minimize the effort required to rewrite the code or manage infrastructure. What should you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Containerize the script. Create a pipeline on Agent Platform Pipelines using the Kubeflow Pipelines (KFP) SDK that executes the container on a machine type with higher memory.

options.label: B
options.text: Provision a Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster. Deploy the dask-kubernetes operator. Update the script to use Dask for distributed dataframe operations that are managed by the team.

options.label: C
options.text: Use the Agent Platform SDK to create a Ray on Agent Platform cluster. Update the script to use Ray Data libraries for distributed processing, and submit the job to the cluster.

options.label: D
options.text: Update the script to use Apache Beam. Run the job on Dataflow.

explanation: Ray on Agent Platform provides a managed, multi-node distributed computing environment through Python-native APIs. Ray Data supports scalable dataframe-style processing, allowing the team to adapt the existing Python workflow with relatively little rewriting while avoiding the operational burden of provisioning and managing a cluster.

question: You work for a large online retailer. You are productionizing a demand forecasting model designed to predict future sales for inventory management. You need to retrain the model with fresh data every 30 days. The inventory planning team requires daily batch predictions for replenishment orders. You need to design a solution that generates daily predictions while minimizing resource costs. Which pipeline architecture should you implement?

options.label: A
options.text: Schedule a pipeline in Agent Platform Pipelines that generates batch predictions daily. Include training as a conditional step that runs if it is day 30 of the cycle.

options.label: B
options.text: Implement two pipelines in Agent Platform Pipelines: a continuous training pipeline that runs every 30 days, and a daily batch prediction pipeline that runs the batch prediction job.

options.label: C
options.text: Implement a pipeline in Agent Platform Pipelines for training that runs every 30 days to update a versioned model on an Agent Platform endpoint. Configure a Cloud Run function to send the daily batch dataset to the endpoint for predictions.

options.label: D
options.text: Implement a pipeline in Agent Platform Pipelines with sequential steps for data preparation, model training, and batch prediction. Schedule the pipeline to run daily.

explanation: Separating training and prediction into independently scheduled pipelines matches the different execution frequencies. The training pipeline updates the model every 30 days, while the batch prediction pipeline uses the latest approved model to generate daily forecasts. This avoids unnecessary daily retraining and minimizes compute costs while keeping predictions current.

question: You work for a financial company that has a large custom dataset with one trillion tokens. The dataset contains financial news, reports, and other related data as well as acquired large public datasets similar to Common Crawl. You need to train a custom LLM from scratch using the open-source open language model (OLMo) framework. You want to maximize throughput. What should you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Store the dataset in Filestore, and create a GKE cluster with a4-highgpu-8g machines (using B200 GPUs). Wrap your PyTorch workflow as a Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) job that you schedule on the cluster.

options.label: B
options.text: Buy a reservation for B200 GPUs. Use Managed Lustre to store the data, and use Cluster Toolkit to create a Slurm cluster with a4-highgpu-8g machines (using B200 GPUs). Schedule a PyTorch training job on this cluster.

options.label: C
options.text: Store the dataset in Filestore, and mount it as NFS. Run an Agent Platform custom training job on B200 GPUs that is based on a PyTorch job.

options.label: D
options.text: Store the dataset in Cloud Storage, and create a Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster using preemptible VMs with a4-highgpu-8g machines (using B200 GPUs). Schedule a PyTorch training job on the cluster.

explanation: A reserved cluster of a4-highgpu-8g machines provides reliable access to NVIDIA B200 GPUs for sustained, large-scale distributed training. Managed Lustre delivers the high-throughput parallel storage needed to feed a trillion-token dataset efficiently, while Cluster Toolkit and Slurm provide an optimized architecture for coordinating multi-node PyTorch workloads and maximizing accelerator utilization.

question: You are developing a Gemini-based onboarding chatbot to answer users’ questions based on five PDF onboarding documents in Cloud Storage. The documents are updated weekly or monthly as needed. You expect that the application will receive high-volume, repeated user queries against this documentation context. You need to use the most appropriate and cost-effective solution for managing the context and ensuring that the chatbot has up-to-date information. What should you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Fine-tune a Gemini model using the text from the five PDF files as a training dataset.

options.label: B
options.text: Send requests with the five PDF files as content pointing to the URI file. Use implicit context caching.

options.label: C
options.text: Create an explicit context cache using the five PDF files, and regenerate the cache when the source files change.

options.label: D
options.text: Create an explicit context cache using the five PDF files. Set a time-to-live (TTL) of seven days, and regenerate the cache every seven days.

explanation: Explicit context caching is designed for high-volume requests that repeatedly use the same large document context, reducing input-processing costs and latency. Recreating the cache whenever the source PDFs change ensures that responses remain grounded in the latest onboarding information without paying to process all five documents with every request.

question: You work for a logistics company that receives thousands of PDF invoices each day from various freight carriers. The invoices are scanned and saved as images in a Cloud Storage bucket. Each invoice contains important information such as invoice number, invoice date, supplier name, and invoice amount. However, the layout and format vary significantly from carrier to carrier. You need to build a pipeline that extracts the fields from all incoming invoices and loads the structured data into a BigQuery table for analysis. You want the solution to be scalable while also minimizing the need for manual data entry and custom parsing logic. What should you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Create a Cloud Run service that uses the Gemini Pro model to read documents to identify and return the required values in JSON format. Create another Cloud Run service to load the JSON files into a Big Query table. Run the Cloud Run services sequentially.

options.label: B
options.text: Use the Cloud Vision API’s OCR feature on a Compute Engine VM to extract all raw text from each document. Write a Python script with regular expressions to search for keywords and parse the extracted text to find the required field values.

options.label: C
options.text: Schedule a notebook in an Agent Platform Workbench instance to periodically train a custom named entity recognition (NER) model on a labeled dataset of invoice documents. Deploy the model to an Agent Platform endpoint, and post-process the model output to write results to a BigQuery table.

options.label: D
options.text: Configure a processor using Document AI’s pre-trained invoice processor, and send each document to its endpoint. Extract the structured entities from the processor’s JSON output.

explanation: Document AI’s pre-trained Invoice Parser is designed to process invoices with varied layouts and extract structured entities such as invoice number, invoice date, supplier name, and invoice amount. It provides scalable document processing and structured JSON output without requiring custom parsing rules or a manually trained model.

question: You developed a demand forecasting model using BigQuery ML. New sales data is ingested into a BigQuery table daily. You want to implement an automated retraining strategy where the model is evaluated against the previous week’s data every Sunday, and the model is retrained if the mean absolute error (MAE) exceeds 500 units. You want to use native BigQuery capabilities to automate this workflow and minimize external dependencies. What should you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Create an Agent Platform Pipelines workflow containing a BigQueryJobOp component that runs the ML.EVALUATE statement. Add a conditional step to check the MAE and conditionally execute a training step. Schedule the pipeline using Agent Platform Pipelines.

options.label: B
options.text: Write a CREATE OR REPLACE MODEL statement with the OPTIONS clause set to warm_start = TRUE. Schedule the query to run every Sunday using a BigQuery scheduled query.

options.label: C
options.text: Create a Cloud Run function triggered by a Cloud Scheduler job. Configure the function to use the BigQuery client library to run the evaluation query. If the MAE threshold is reached, issue a second API call to retrain the model.

options.label: D
options.text: Use BigQuery procedural language to write a query that runs the ML.EVALUATE statement, stores the MAE in a variable, and uses an IF statement to conditionally execute the CREATE OR REPLACE MODEL statement. Schedule the script using a BigQuery scheduled query.

explanation: BigQuery procedural SQL can evaluate the model, assign the resulting MAE to a variable, and use conditional logic to retrain only when the threshold is exceeded. Scheduling the script as a weekly BigQuery scheduled query keeps the entire workflow within BigQuery and minimizes external services and dependencies.

question: You work in the credit card fraud detection department of a bank that processes millions of transactions per day. You need to create and serve a real-time fraud detection model. To address the challenge of feature engineering at this scale with limited raw data, you plan to create time-related aggregate features, such as the average transaction amount within the last month or the amount of time since the last transaction. How should you process the data for model training and serving?

options.label: A
options.text: Ingest the transaction data into BigQuery. Use the TRANSFORM clause in BigQuery ML to create new features by applying SQL functions to the raw transaction data.

options.label: B
options.text: Create streaming Dataflow pipelines that read transaction data from Pub/Sub. Use a windowing function to aggregate transaction data over time. Store the engineered features in Agent Platform Feature Store.

options.label: C
options.text: Ingest the transaction data into BigQuery. Use a TRANSFORM_ONLY model in BigQuery ML to create a reusable feature engineering pipeline. Use this pipeline to preprocess the data.

options.label: D
options.text: Orchestrate a workflow in Agent Platform Pipelines that exports raw transaction data from BigQuery to Cloud Storage. Perform feature engineering using a Python script in a custom component in the pipeline.

explanation: A streaming Dataflow pipeline can process millions of transaction events from Pub/Sub and use stateful, windowed aggregations to calculate time-dependent features such as monthly average transaction amounts and time since the previous transaction. Storing these engineered values in Agent Platform Feature Store makes consistent features available for both model training and low-latency online serving.

question:
You are part of a team of ML engineers building a new churn prediction model using PyTorch. Your team’s raw data is stored in BigQuery. For the initial prototyping phase, your team needs a collaborative, cloud-based environment that meets the following criteria:
● It must provide access to GPU accelerators.
● It must allow seamless authentication to BigQuery without manual management of service account keys.
● It must be pre-configured with common ML frameworks.
You need to choose the most secure solution with the least setup overhead for your team to begin model development and experimentation. What should you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Configure a JupyterHub server on a cluster of Compute Engine instances. Install the necessary GPU drivers and other required libraries on each instance. Instruct each team member to create and download a service account key for BigQuery access.

options.label: B
options.text: Package the PyTorch model code in a Docker container, and upload it to Artifact Registry. Use Agent Platform Serverless Training to run a custom training job that runs on a GPU-enabled machine type. Instruct the team to analyze the training logs to iterate on the model.

options.label: C
options.text: Instruct team members to use the free version of Agent Platform Colab Enterprise. Use the Agent Platform SDK for Python to load the data into a shared Agent Platform Colab Enterprise notebook. Have each member perform analysis in the shared notebook.

options.label: D
options.text: Create Agent Platform Workbench instances for your team members. Select instance types with attached GPUs and the preinstalled PyTorch kernel. Use the BigQuery client library to access the data, and use the instances’ managed identity for authentication.

explanation: Agent Platform Workbench provides managed Jupyter environments with GPU-enabled machine types and preconfigured PyTorch kernels. Its managed identity enables secure access to BigQuery through Application Default Credentials, eliminating the need to create, distribute, or maintain service account keys while minimizing setup effort for collaborative experimentation.

question: You are responsible for managing the recommendation engine on an ecommerce website. The current model is deployed on a public Agent Platform endpoint and is actively serving production traffic. You have developed an updated version of the model and registered the model in Model Registry. You need to perform an A/B test to compare the new model’s performance to the current model. You plan to implement a traffic split, routing 10% of all incoming production requests to the new model and sending the remaining 90% to the current model. You want this transition to be transparent, and require no modifications to the client application that calls the endpoint. What should you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Deploy the new model to a serverless Cloud Run service. Implement logic in the client application that routes 10% of user requests to the Cloud Run service and the rest to the original endpoint.

options.label: B
options.text: Deploy the new model to the Agent Platform endpoint where the current model is deployed. Configure the endpoint’s traffic split to allocate 10% of user requests to the new model.

options.label: C
options.text: Create two separate Agent Platform Pipelines, one for each model version. Use Agent Platform Experiments to run both pipelines simultaneously. Configure the experiment to send 10% of user requests to the new model’s pipeline and the rest to the production model’s pipeline.

options.label: D
options.text: Deploy the new model to a new Agent Platform endpoint. Configure Cloud Load Balancing to send 10% of user requests to the new endpoint and the rest to the original endpoint.

explanation: Deploying both model versions to the same Agent Platform endpoint allows the endpoint’s native traffic-splitting configuration to route 10% of prediction requests to the new model and 90% to the current model. The endpoint URL remains unchanged, so the A/B test requires no client application modifications.

question: You are the lead ML engineer for a large ecommerce company. The Data Analytics team has prepared a dataset of 50 million transaction rows, which is stored in a partitioned BigQuery table. The team consists primarily of SQL experts with limited experience in Python or TensorFlow. You need to build a binary classification model to predict the likelihood of a customer making a purchase in the next seven days. You need to provide daily batch predictions. You need to minimize development effort, data movement, and the overall complexity of the solution. What should you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Create a model with BigQuery ML that includes the MODEL_TYPE=AUTOML_CLASSIFIER settings. Use the ML.PREDICT function to generate predictions as part of your nightly data warehouse jobs.

options.label: B
options.text: Use the BigQuery ML TRANSFORM function to normalize and scale numerical features, one-hot encode categorical features, and train a MODEL_TYPE=LOGISTIC_REG mode. Use the ML.PREDICT function to generate predictions as part of your nightly data warehouse jobs.

options.label: C
options.text: Train a classification model with Agent Platform AutoML Tabular Workflows, deploy the trained model to an Agent Platform endpoint, and add a nightly Cloud Run job to trigger batch predictions.

options.label: D
options.text: Develop an XGBoost model on an Agent Platform Workbench notebook. Load the data into a pandas DataFrame, and pickle it to a Cloud Storage bucket. Create another notebook that loads the pickled model from Cloud Storage and saves predictions back to Cloud Storage. Schedule this notebook for nightly execution.

explanation: BigQuery ML AutoML classification allows the SQL-focused team to train a high-quality binary classifier directly on the 50-million-row BigQuery table without moving the data or developing custom Python training code. ML.PREDICT can be integrated into existing nightly warehouse jobs to generate daily batch predictions entirely within BigQuery, minimizing operational complexity and development effort.

question: You have deployed a deep learning model to an Agent Platform endpoint using a machine type with NVIDIA GPUs. You initially configured the endpoint to autoscale based on a target CPU utilization of 60%. During a load test, you observe that prediction latency increases significantly as traffic rises, but the number of replicas remains constant. Cloud Monitoring indicates that CPU utilization stays below 40%, while the GPU utilization consistently exceeds 90%. You need to ensure that the endpoint scales efficiently to handle the increased load. What should you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Update the autoscaling configuration to scale based on the GPU duty cycle metric.

options.label: B
options.text: Update the autoscaling configuration to decrease the target CPU utilization to 20%.

options.label: C
options.text: Redeploy the model to a machine type that includes a TPU.

options.label: D
options.text: Increase the minimum replica count for the endpoint to match the peak load that was observed during testing.

explanation: The endpoint is constrained by GPU capacity rather than CPU capacity. Configuring autoscaling to use GPU duty cycle allows replica count to increase when GPU utilization becomes high, directly responding to the resource causing prediction latency.

question: Your company manages an ecommerce platform and has a large dataset of customer reviews. Each review has a positive, negative, or neutral label. You need to quickly prototype a sentiment analysis model that accurately predicts the sentiment labels of new customer reviews while minimizing time and cost. What should you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Use the Agent Platform Text Embeddings API to vectorize the text, and train a regression model by using Agent Platform AutoML to predict sentiment scores.

options.label: B
options.text: Use Agent Platform AutoML to train a multi-class classification model that predicts sentiment labels based on the training data.

options.label: C
options.text: Use the Natural Language API for real-time sentiment analysis.

options.label: D
options.text: Train a sentiment analysis model by using a BERT-based model, and fine-tune the model by using domain-specific customer reviews.

explanation: Agent Platform AutoML can train a multi-class text classification model directly from the labeled customer reviews. It minimizes custom coding, infrastructure management, and tuning effort while producing predictions for the positive, negative, and neutral sentiment classes.

question: You are an enterprise AI architect in a large international company. An ML team has asked you to help with development of a pilot of a customer support bot. The ML team plans to use the DeepSeek-V3.2 model, and they expect a few hundred requests per day. You need to quickly deploy the model using a cost-efficient approach. What should you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Use the DeepSeek-V3.2 model as a service (MaaS) in Model Garden. Send HTTP requests in the Agent Platform endpoint using the Python requests library.

options.label: B
options.text: Download the DeepSeek-V3.2 binaries from Model Garden, and deploy the model on a Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) Autoscaling cluster. Send HTTP requests to the GKE endpoint using the Python requests library.

options.label: C
options.text: Navigate to the DeepSeek-V3.2 model card in Model Garden. Click “Deploy model” to deploy it as an Agent Platform endpoint. Invoke the endpoint using the aiplatform SDK.

options.label: D
options.text: Use the DeepSeek-V3.2 model as a service (MaaS) in Model Garden. Use a Python client from the openai SDK, and pass a custom endpoint URL to the client.

explanation: Using DeepSeek-V3.2 as a managed model-as-a-service provides serverless, pay-per-use inference without provisioning or maintaining GPU infrastructure, making it cost-efficient for a pilot with only a few hundred daily requests. The managed endpoint supports the OpenAI Python SDK by configuring the Agent Platform endpoint as the client’s base URL.

question: You have a high-traffic ecommerce application that uses a recommendation model deployed on an Agent Platform endpoint. During flash sales, traffic quickly spikes from 1,000 to 50,000 queries per second (QPS). During these spikes, the application returns 503: Service Unavailable errors because the autoscaler cannot provision new resources quickly enough to meet the sudden demand. Your need to eliminate service disruptions during the start of the sale. How should you configure the endpoint?

options.label: A
options.text: Change the machine type to an a2-highgpu-1g instance with an NVIDIA A100 GPU.

options.label: B
options.text: Increase the min_replica_count to a baseline that covers a significant portion of the expected spike, and set the max_replica_count to 100.

options.label: C
options.text: Set the min_replica_count to 1 and the max_replica_count to 100 in the deployed model’s automatic scaling configuration.

options.label: D
options.text: Deploy the model to a private Agent Platform endpoint, and autoscale based on GPU utilization.

explanation: Increasing the minimum replica count pre-provisions enough serving capacity to absorb the initial traffic surge before autoscaling can add more replicas. Setting a sufficiently high maximum replica count then allows the endpoint to continue scaling as demand grows, preventing startup-period 503 errors during flash sales.

question: You lead an ML team at a financial technology company. Your team is building a system to detect potentially fraudulent credit card transactions in real-time. The model must return a prediction with very low latency (under 200ms) to approve or deny the transaction. The system must also scale to handle millions of transactions per day. Your dataset consists of structured, tabular transaction data stored in BigQuery. Your team is proficient in data science but wants to avoid the complexity of managing and optimizing a real-time model serving infrastructure. What should you do?

options.label: A
options.text: In an Agent Platform Workbench notebook, build a deep neural network (DNN) using PyTorch. Provision a cluster of GPU-enabled Compute Engine instances, and create an API to serve the model for real-time predictions.

options.label: B
options.text: Use BigQuery ML to train a boosted tree classification model. Schedule a batch prediction job using the ML.PREDICT function that runs every minute and scores recent transactions.

options.label: C
options.text: Use Forecasting with Agent Platform AutoML to train a time-series model on the sequence of transactions. Deploy the model as a tabular workflow to predict which future time windows are likely to contain fraudulent activity.

options.label: D
options.text: Use Agent Platform AutoML to train using your tabular dataset from BigQuery. Deploy the trained model to an Agent Platform endpoint, and integrate the endpoint’s API into your transaction processing application.

explanation: Agent Platform AutoML can train an accurate classification model directly from structured BigQuery data while minimizing custom model-development effort. Deploying the trained model to a managed Agent Platform endpoint provides low-latency online predictions, autoscaling, and managed serving infrastructure suitable for millions of real-time transaction requests.

question: You are training a ResNet-50 computer vision model on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform using a custom PyTorch container. The training job is configured with a generic machine type and one NVIDIA A100 GPU. During the training, you monitor the resource utilization charts. You observe that the GPU utilization is volatile, frequently dropping to 0% for short intervals, while the CPU utilization remains consistently above 90%. You want to maximize GPU utilization to reduce training time. What should you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Increase the training batch size to saturate the GPU memory.

options.label: B
options.text: Update the DataLoader utility to increase the num_workers parameter and enable pin_memory.

options.label: C
options.text: Switch to a machine type with a higher number of GPUs, and implement the torch.nn.parallel.DistributedDataParallel strategy in the training code.

options.label: D
options.text: Enable automatic mixed precision (AMP) to speed up the matrix multiplications.

explanation: The consistently high CPU utilization and intermittent GPU idle periods indicate that data loading and preprocessing cannot supply batches fast enough. Increasing parallel data-loading workers and using pinned memory improves CPU-side throughput and accelerates host-to-GPU transfers, keeping the GPU fed more consistently and reducing training time.

question: You work at a marketing research firm. Your team’s current project involves analyzing a large volume of customer surveys. Your team decides to use LLMs in Model Garden and track model training artifacts. You need to determine how to effectively share notebooks within your team and how to orchestrate the ML workflow. You want to use Google-managed services as much as possible. What should you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Develop your code in Agent Platform Colab Enterprise, and orchestrate your ML workflow by using Agent Platform Pipelines.

options.label: B
options.text: Develop your code in Agent Platform Colab Enterprise, and orchestrate your ML workflow by using Cloud Workflows.

options.label: C
options.text: Develop your code in Agent Platform Workbench, and orchestrate your ML workflow by using Cloud Build.

options.label: D
options.text: Develop your code in Agent Platform Workbench, and orchestrate your ML workflow by using Agent Platform Pipelines.

explanation: Agent Platform Colab Enterprise provides a Google-managed, collaborative notebook environment that simplifies sharing work across the team. Agent Platform Pipelines is the managed orchestration service for repeatable ML workflows and integrates with training jobs, Model Garden resources, metadata, and model artifacts.

question: You are building an ML workflow that preprocesses data, trains a model with hyperparameter tuning, and deploys the best model to an Agent Platform endpoint. Your preprocessing step takes two hours and outputs a 100 GB dataset. You run experiments daily with different model architectures using the same preprocessing step. You need to automate this process and optimize the pipeline runs to minimize cost and time. What should you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Configure an Agent Platform Pipelines workflow with a single component for the preprocessing and training steps. Use Agent Platform hyperparameter tuning jobs within the component to identify optimal parameters.

options.label: B
options.text: Configure an Agent Platform Pipelines workflow with separate components for the preprocessing and training steps. Enable caching on the preprocessing component, and use Agent Platform Serverless Training custom jobs for the training steps.

options.label: C
options.text: Configure an Agent Platform Pipelines workflow with separate components for the preprocessing and training steps. Use a Cloud Run function to trigger the pipeline, and configure Agent Platform Serverless Training custom jobs for the training steps.

options.label: D
options.text: Configure an Agent Platform Pipelines workflow that starts with an Agent Platform Serverless Training custom job for the preprocessing step. Use a Cloud Run function to launch the hyperparameter tuning job that is triggered when the preprocessed data arrives in Cloud Storage.

explanation: Separating preprocessing and training allows the pipeline to cache the expensive preprocessing output. Because the input data and preprocessing configuration remain unchanged across daily architecture experiments, subsequent runs can reuse the 100 GB artifact instead of repeating the two-hour step. Serverless custom training jobs then provide managed, scalable execution for each training experiment.

question: You are an ML engineer at a retail company. You need to automate a recurring retraining workflow for a demand forecasting model. The workflow involves dependencies across hybrid environments and must execute the following sequential steps: 1. Trigger a shell script on an on-premises server to extract legacy sales data and send it to a Cloud Storage bucket. 2. Trigger a pipeline in Agent Platform Pipelines to train and validate the new model. 3. Push the validation metrics to a third-party API. You need a fully managed orchestration service that provides native connectors to handle these cross-platform dependencies. You want to use the most stable, robust solution. What should you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Use Workflows to define the orchestration logic in YAML. Use the http.post connector to trigger the on-premises shell script and the Agent Platform API for the training job.

options.label: B
options.text: Use Cloud Scheduler to trigger a Cloud Run function that executes the on-premises script using SSH, publishes a Pub/Sub message upon completion, and triggers the subsequent workflow steps.

options.label: C
options.text: Use Managed Service for Apache Airflow to define a directed acyclic graph (DAG) in Python. Use Apache Airflow operators and sensors to orchestrate the workflow steps.

options.label: D
options.text: Use Agent Platform Pipelines to develop a custom container component for each workflow step. Use the Kubeflow Pipelines (KFP) SDK to define the execution order.

explanation: Managed Service for Apache Airflow is a fully managed orchestration platform designed for complex data and ML workflows spanning on-premises, Google Cloud, and external services. An Airflow DAG can use operators and sensors to execute the legacy extraction, wait for completion, launch the training pipeline, and submit metrics to the external API with robust dependency management, retries, monitoring, and failure handling.

question: You are developing an automated training workflow using Agent Platform Pipelines. The pipeline trains a new custom model and registers it to Model Registry. You need to validate the model’s performance on a held-out test dataset. You want to ensure that the model is deployed to a production Agent Platform endpoint only if its evaluation metrics meet a specific threshold. You want to minimize cost and administrative overhead. What should you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Configure the training component to calculate evaluation metrics on the training dataset during the training job. Output the metrics to the next step and use a conditional task to deploy the model if the evaluation metrics exceed the specified threshold.

options.label: B
options.text: Insert a Python component that pulls the latest model version from Model Registry. Compare its training metrics against the current production model, and use a conditional task to deploy the new model if it performs better.

options.label: C
options.text: Deploy the model to a temporary Agent Platform endpoint. Use a custom component to send the test dataset for online prediction, calculate the metrics, and deploy to the production endpoint if the evaluation metrics exceed the specified threshold.

options.label: D
options.text: Add a batch prediction component to generate predictions on the test dataset. Pass the results to a model evaluation component. Use a conditional task to deploy the model if the evaluation metrics exceed the specified threshold.

explanation: Batch prediction evaluates the newly trained model against the held-out test dataset without provisioning an online endpoint. A dedicated evaluation component can calculate the required metrics, and the pipeline can use those outputs in a conditional task so deployment occurs only when the defined performance threshold is met.

question: You are developing a machine learning pipeline using the Kubeflow Pipelines (KFP) SDK that will run on Agent Platform Pipelines. The pipeline includes a preprocessing component that takes two hours to transform a large dataset. You are currently iterating on the code for the subsequent model_training component and need to resubmit the pipeline frequently for testing. You need to ensure that the preprocessing component only re-runs if its inputs or parameters have changed. You want to minimize effort, costs, and total execution time. What should you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Ensure that execution caching is enabled for the preprocessing component by including the set_caching_options(enable_caching=True) method.

options.label: B
options.text: Track the run lineage using Agent Platform Experiments, and pass the output artifact URI from the previous run into the training component.

options.label: C
options.text: Configure the pipeline to write the preprocessed data to a persistent volume claim (PVC) that is shared across pipeline runs.

options.label: D
options.text: Add a dsl.Condition step to the pipeline that checks if the preprocessing step has executed in the last hour.

explanation: Execution caching reuses the preprocessing component’s previous successful output when its inputs, parameters, and component definition have not changed. This prevents the two-hour transformation from running during repeated pipeline tests, reducing both execution time and compute cost.

question: You are an ML engineer at a large retail company. You have a BigQuery table containing five years of daily sales data for 50,000 distinct product SKUs. You need to generate a daily demand forecast for the next 30 days for each individual SKU. The solution must automatically account for holidays and weekly seasonality. You want to minimize data egress costs and operational complexity by keeping the data and model within the data warehouse. What should you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Use the CREATE MODEL... OPTIONS(model_type='ARIMA_PLUS') statement in BigQuery to generate a forecast based on historical SKU sales.

options.label: B
options.text: Use the gcloud ai custom-jobs create command to run a PyTorch LSTM container on Agent Platform that pulls data from a CSV into Cloud Storage.

options.label: C
options.text: Use the CREATE MODEL... OPTIONS(model_type='LINEAR_REG') statement in BigQuery to predict sales using the transaction date as a feature.

options.label: D
options.text: Use the google-cloud-aiplatform SDK to create a TimeSeriesDataset and trigger an AutoMLForecastingTrainingJob.

explanation: BigQuery ML ARIMA_PLUS trains and forecasts directly within BigQuery, avoiding data movement and separate serving infrastructure. By specifying the SKU as the time-series identifier, one model can generate independent 30-day forecasts for all 50,000 products while automatically detecting seasonal patterns and modeling holiday effects.

question: Your team is deploying a real-time personalized ad-ranking model. The model requires low-latency access for hundreds of user-level features to be fetched at request time. These features are stored in BigQuery and updated frequently by a streaming Dataflow pipeline. As your user base continues to grow, you discover that fetching these features from BigQuery at request time is causing the total inference latency to exceed your 100 ms SLA. You need a feature serving layer that provides low-latency retrieval and scales automatically while minimizing operational overhead. What should you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Use the BigQueryReadClient to stream data directly into the model’s inference container.

options.label: B
options.text: Enable Agent Platform Feature Store, and use the FetchFeatureValues API to fetch features for the model.

options.label: C
options.text: Implement a Redis cache on Memorystore, and add a component to the Dataflow pipeline to write the feature to the Redis cache.

options.label: D
options.text: Use BigQuery BI Engine to accelerate the SQL queries used to fetch features.

explanation: Agent Platform Feature Store provides a managed online serving layer for low-latency feature retrieval at prediction time. The FetchFeatureValues API can return frequently updated user features with substantially lower latency than querying BigQuery directly, while automatically scaling and avoiding the operational burden of managing a custom cache.

question: You are optimizing the training of a 175-billion parameter LLM on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform. You have provisioned a TPU v5p Pod slice with 32 chips for the job. You initially ran the training using standard data parallelism, but the job immediately failed with an out-of-memory (OOM) error. You need to implement a training strategy that resolves the memory issue and minimizes training latency. What should you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Configure the training to use a parameter server architecture where the model weights are stored in the host CPU memory.

options.label: B
options.text: Enable gradient checkpointing, and continue using the data parallelism strategy.

options.label: C
options.text: Configure the training to shard the model parameters and optimizer states, and continue using the data parallelism strategy.

options.label: D
options.text: Scale up the TPU Pod slice to include more chips, and continue using the data parallelism strategy.

explanation: Sharding the model parameters and optimizer states across the TPU chips distributes the memory footprint instead of replicating the full 175-billion-parameter model on every device. This resolves the out-of-memory failure while retaining data parallelism for high-throughput training and lower overall training latency.

question: You have deployed a custom classification model to an Agent Platform endpoint to predict the likelihood of customer churn in real-time. You need to collect the data to calculate the model’s exact precision and recall by comparing production predictions with ground truth data in BigQuery. You want to minimize development effort. What should you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Modify the prediction container to asynchronously write the prediction result to BigQuery after every request.

options.label: B
options.text: Schedule a daily Agent Platform batch prediction job that uses the same model resource as the deployed endpoint and stores predictions in BigQuery.

options.label: C
options.text: Update the model deployment parameters to enable request-response logging to BigQuery. Set the sampling rate to 1.0.

options.label: D
options.text: Create a model evaluation job by providing the model resource and the BigQuery ground truth table to calculate precision and recall.

explanation: Request-response logging automatically records every online prediction request and response in BigQuery when the sampling rate is set to 1.0. These logged predictions can then be joined with the ground truth data to calculate exact production precision and recall without modifying the serving container or building a separate prediction workflow.

question: You are in the exploratory phase of development of a demand forecasting model. Several terabytes of historical sales and inventory records are stored in a BigQuery table. You need to create a new, clean table to perform preliminary analyses on metrics, such as moving averages of sales figures and weekly aggregates, without additional data movement. You want to use the simplest approach and minimize overhead. What should you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Create a PreprocessingOp component in the Agent Platform Pipelines workflow to compute the moving averages and extract time-based features and write the processed data to a new destination table in BigQuery.

options.label: B
options.text: Read the data from BigQuery into a Dask DataFrame using Agent Platform Workbench. Perform exploratory data analysis (EDA) and feature engineering transformations, and write the processed data back to a new destination table in BigQuery.

options.label: C
options.text: Write a SQL query in the BigQuery console. Use the ML.TRANSFORM function in BigQuery ML to compute the moving averages and extract time-based features. Write the processed data to a new destination table in BigQuery.

options.label: D
options.text: Write a SQL query in the BigQuery console. Use standard SQL functions like CAST, EXTRACT, and window functions with OVER() clauses to perform the transformations and calculations. Materialize the results into a new destination table in BigQuery.

explanation: BigQuery standard SQL can calculate moving averages with window functions, create weekly aggregates, and derive date-based features directly where the data resides. Materializing the query results into a new BigQuery table avoids data movement and additional ML or pipeline infrastructure, making it the simplest and lowest-overhead approach.

question: You work for a healthcare organization and need to automate the patient triage process. You want to build a telephony agentic solution using the Gemini Live API to perform human-like conversations with patients and gather necessary patient information. You plan to pilot the solution in Japanese. You need to minimize latency and development time, and ensure high, native-like fluency in the model’s responses. What should you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Use Gemini Live API Speech-to-Text functionality to capture the user’s input followed by Text-to-Speech streaming processing with Chirp to communicate with the patient in their language.

options.label: B
options.text: Use the Gemini Live API, and configure the language_code field to ja-JP. Include a clear system instruction to respond in the patient’s language.

options.label: C
options.text: Fine-tune the Gemini Flash model on a dataset of Japanese medical transcripts to ensure native fluency. Deploy this custom model behind the Gemini Live API.

options.label: D
options.text: Use the Gemini Pro model to automatically select the appropriate language.

explanation: The Gemini Live API provides native, real-time audio interaction without a separate speech-to-text and text-to-speech pipeline, minimizing conversational latency and development effort. Configuring Japanese as the language and adding a clear system instruction guides the model to maintain fluent, natural Japanese throughout the patient interaction.

question: You work for an international bank. Your team is developing a generative AI application that summarizes complex financial reports. You need to implement an automated, scalable solution to evaluate and quantify the quality of generated summaries against the previous version of the solution. What should you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Use Model Monitoring to track the prediction drift of the token output length.

options.label: B
options.text: Run an automatic side-by-side (AutoSxS) evaluation job in Agent Platform to compare outputs from the new and previous versions of the solution.

options.label: C
options.text: Deploy both versions of the solution, and use A/B testing to route a portion of production traffic to the new version and route the remaining traffic to the previous version. Compare user click-through rates.

options.label: D
options.text: Run an evaluation job in Agent Platform, and calculate a BLEU score to compare the new and previous versions of the solution.

explanation: Automatic side-by-side evaluation is designed to compare the generated outputs of two model or application versions at scale. It uses an automated evaluator to assess relative response quality across the same prompt set, providing quantitative comparison results without requiring manual review or production traffic experiments.

question: You are using generative AI to build a conversational agent to support bank customers’ inquiries about their product base and transaction history. You must ensure that the agent does not include personally identifiable information (PII) in its responses. You want to implement this requirement with minimal effort. What should you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Configure the safety_settings thresholds within the Agent Platform model parameters to Block_Most.

options.label: B
options.text: Develop a post-processing wrapper using Python’s re module with patterns r'\b(?:\d{4}[- ]?) {3}\d{4}\b' to identify and redact credit card numbers.

options.label: C
options.text: Implement Model Armor with Sensitive Data Protection to detect and redact PII from the agent’s responses.

options.label: D
options.text: Use sampled Shapley (SHAP) values to understand the model’s predictions and ensure that it is not biased toward revealing PII.

explanation: Model Armor integrates with Sensitive Data Protection to inspect generated responses for personally identifiable information and automatically redact or block sensitive content. This provides managed, policy-based protection across multiple PII types with minimal custom development.

question: You work for a media company. You are developing a solution that requires transcription and diarizing (speaker identification) of live audio streams in near real-time. You are using an optimized WhisperX model built on the PyTorch framework that uses several libraries and weights sourced from the Hugging Face Hub. The deployment must include proprietary Python post-processing logic including speaker diarization and alignment correction that executes immediately after model inference. You need your solution to be efficient, scalable, handle high throughput, and minimize serving latency. How should you deploy this model and its required logic?

options.label: A
options.text: Deploy the WhisperX model artifacts to an Agent Platform endpoint using a pre-built PyTorch serving container configured with a GPU. Host the custom post-processing scripts in a Cloud Run function that receives the endpoint’s prediction output and performs the final diarization.

options.label: B
options.text: Use a self-managed Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster for deployment. Package the model and logic into a container, and configure the cluster’s horizontal pod autoscaler (HPA) to manage throughput.

options.label: C
options.text: Package the WhisperX model artifacts, the specific Python post-processing scripts, and the necessary dependencies (including Hugging Face libraries) into a single, custom serving container image. Deploy this custom image to a GPU-enabled Agent Platform endpoint.

options.label: D
options.text: Locate the WhisperX model in the Model Garden and use the “1-click deploy” feature to deploy it to an Agent Platform endpoint. Route the output to a Dataflow pipeline that uses a custom DoFn function to handle the post-processing and logging.

explanation: A custom serving container can bundle the optimized WhisperX model, Hugging Face dependencies, model weights, and proprietary diarization and alignment logic into one inference service. Deploying that container to a GPU-enabled Agent Platform endpoint provides managed autoscaling and high-throughput serving while keeping post-processing in the same request path, which minimizes data transfer and end-to-end latency.

question: You manage an ML workflow for a fraud detection model. The source code for data processing and model training is stored in a version control repository. You need to implement a continuous training (CT) pipeline that automatically runs unit tests and launches a new training run on Agent Platform Pipelines when code is updated in the repository. You want to use a fully managed service to orchestrate this process. What should you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Create a Cloud Run function that is triggered by repository commits. The function runs the unit tests, launches a custom training job, and uses Model Monitoring to validate the new model’s performance before deployment.

options.label: B
options.text: Define a Cloud Workflow to monitor the repository for changes. Configure the workflow on Agent Platform Pipelines to orchestrate and run the unit tests. Use the model evaluation component to validate the new model’s performance before deployment.

options.label: C
options.text: Configure Agent Platform Pipelines to poll the repository for updates. Add a conditional step in the pipeline that uses Model Monitoring to validate the new model’s performance before deployment.

options.label: D
options.text: Create a Cloud Build trigger associated with the repository. Define a build configuration file that runs the unit tests and triggers a job on Agent Platform Pipelines. Use the model evaluation component to validate the model performance before deployment.

explanation: Cloud Build provides fully managed, repository-triggered CI automation. A build trigger can run unit tests whenever code changes are committed and, after successful validation, invoke the Agent Platform Pipeline for retraining. The pipeline can then evaluate the new model before allowing deployment.

question: You are deploying a generative AI chatbot for an online gaming community using Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform. During beta testing, you discover that users are able to input malicious prompts that cause the model to generate hate speech and violent content. You need to implement a guardrail to block this content in production with minimal development overhead. What should you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Update the system instruction (system prompt) of the model to explicitly state: “You are a helpful assistant. Do not generate hate speech or violent content.”

options.label: B
options.text: Implement and configure Model Armor to sanitize responses if hateful content is detected.

options.label: C
options.text: Create a supervised fine-tuning (SFT) job in Agent Platform, and tune the model using a curated dataset of safe, policy-compliant gaming conversations.

options.label: D
options.text: Integrate the Cloud Natural Language API’s moderation capabilities to analyze and block toxic user prompts before they reach the chatbot model.

explanation: Model Armor provides a managed guardrail that inspects prompts and responses for unsafe content, including hate speech and violence, and can block or sanitize detected content. It reduces development and maintenance effort compared with building custom moderation logic or relying only on prompting.
